summary.text: An 84-year-old man had chronic kidney disease since 2010, hyperlipidemia on atorvastatin, impaired glucose tolerance from 2014 and coronary artery disease from 2017 with long-term aspirin.

In early February 2024 he developed an intermittent cough with blood-streaked sputum, sore throat, dry mouth, arthralgia, fatigue and occasional low fever, then dark red urine on the morning of February 14 and emergency department admission. Admission CT showed patchy lung shadows, creatinine was 293 μmol/L, and the provisional diagnosis was pneumonia, acute-on-chronic kidney disease and hematuria.

He worsened with fever to 39℃, bright red hemoptysis, reduced bright red urine, petechiae and ecchymoses. On February 18 C-ANCA was positive with PR3 above 200 RU/mL and creatinine 457 μmol/L, and AAV was diagnosed with ANCA-associated nephritis not excluded. That night he developed orthopnea with wet rales, and on February 19 CT showed marked bilateral changes with troponin and NT-proBNP elevated and ST depression.

Treatment began with antibiotics, then meropenem and caspofungin, CRRT, and methylprednisolone with cyclophosphamide, which was stopped after trilineage cytopenia on February 22. Double filtration plasmapheresis, oral methylprednisolone tapering, low-dose rituximab induction on March 1 to 3, further plasma exchange on March 19 to 21, a weekly rituximab course from April 3, mycophenolate with sulfamethoxazole on May 23 and belimumab on June 14 and 18 followed. A renal biopsy was not performed because consent was declined.

PR3 antibody fell, hemoptysis, hematuria and ecchymoses resolved, lung CT improved, and he avoided mechanical ventilation. After 6 months of treatment he achieved clinical, radiological and serological remission with ANCA 150 IU/L on August 22, a Birmingham Vasculitis Activity Score of 2, stable pre-dialysis creatinine and discontinuation of hemodialysis, and was successfully discharged.
